In the uplink, the standard includes OFDMA based scheduled access in which the associated stations can be scheduled by an 802.11ax access point (AP). The quality of service for the associated stations can therefore be enhanced by intelligent scheduling of the stations on the OFDMA uplink. The AP is responsible for partitioning the available spectrum to resource units, allocating the resource units to the stations, and transmit power control at the station. In this paper, we consider the design of joint policies for resource unit allocation and power control for the 802.11ax uplink with the objective of minimizing the average latency (or average queue length) of packets queued at the station destined for the AP, while the average transmit power is constrained. Using the drift plus penalty approach we propose two heuristic scheduling policies for the above problem. The achievable average queue lengths and average powers for these scheduling policies are obtained using simulations.

articleTitle: An asymmetrical slot circularly polarized on-chip antenna for wireless SoC applications at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized on-chip antenna has been proposed for system on chip (SoC) applications at ISM 2.45 GHz band. The low resistive and high permittivity silicon (Si) wafer (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\rho=10\ \Omega.\mathrm{cm}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=11.9$</tex>) with standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS technology has been considered for the design of on-chip antenna. The proposed slotted on-chip antenna (OCA) has the miniaturized dimension of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\times 25\times 0.3795\ \mathrm{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The introduction of asymmetry in slot of OCA results enhancement of the directive gain of +4.65 dB and also provide the circular polarization (CP). The 10 dB bandwidth i.e. FBW (Fractional bandwidth) of the proposed antenna is 62.8%. The proposed antenna also shows very good axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 12.98% from 2.31-2.51 GHz range. All the simulation results have been depicted and explained in various sections of the paper.

articleTitle: A simulation based study to identify optimal number of controllers for multi-application scenarios in Software Defined Wireless Sensor Network (SDWSN)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Software Defined Network (SDN) is an effective way of implementing modularity based on abstraction for complex networking principles. SDN has shown its positive impact on various types of networks and the use of SDN in MEMS (Microelectronic Mechanicals Systems) based network also known as Wireless Sensor Network (WSN), helps to alleviate WSN challenges such as less power consumption and better throughput. So far, study on optimal number of controllers and their impact on network parameters remain untouched. In this paper, we follow a simulation-based approach to identify the optimal number of SDN controllers required to manage nodes in WSN. We consider a network of nodes as well as a WSN sink and randomly assign multiple nodes with SDN functionality. We varied the number of controllers and their location for multi-application scenarios. Results show that a) The optimal number of controllers are dependent on the number of applications and nature of application assigned to WSN, b) Presence of SDN controllers increases network lifetime in terms of the amount of residual energy left on the nodes, and c) Selecting appropriate path and assigning routes to WSN nodes by SDN controller increases the overall application throughput.

articleTitle: Integrated Framework for Farmer Centric Agriculture Applications Using IoT Architectures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Role of Internet of Things (IoT) in Agriculture is predominant over the past several years. Knowledge bases of new technological trends in agriculture can help farmers in real time to increase the productivity of whole chain of agriculture processes. Timely suggestions and automation in certain areas of the agriculture industry is possible by connecting farmers, knowledge bases, experts, sensors, actuators, markets and other factors using evolving technologies like IoT. End-to-end platforms to increase the qualitative and quantitative Agriculture production is essential to transform agriculture into a more profitable sector. In this context, a integrated framework is proposed in this paper with a combination of modern technologies like IoT, Mobile and Android software modules that can address most of the above issues. Proposed framework automates the process of connecting, communicating and conveying different aspects of efficient and economic agriculture practices by empowering even the illiterate farmers with latest mobile GUI. Suggestion module from experts relating diseases, water requirements, Data anaysis and forecasting module and Farmers Ecommerce are some of the value Add-on applications integrated into the proposed framework. Developed framework is tested with some of the test cases and future scope of the improvements for the developed framework are given in this paper.

articleTitle: Secrecy Analysis of MRC Diversity Schemes over Nakagami-m Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the secrecy performance of maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity scheme over Nakagami-m fading channels. Closed form expressions for probability of existence of positive secrecy (PEPS) and lower bound on secrecy outage probability (SOP) are derived. We also analyse the secrecy diversity order of the system and concluded that the secrecy diversity order is m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sub>. The derived expressions are validated by the results obtained from Monte Carlo simulations. The lower bound on SOP evaluated from the derived expressions are found accurately tight from the excellent agreement between analytical and simulation results.

Author Keywords: Physical layer security for wireless communication
probability of existence of positive secrecy

articleTitle: Preserving Users' Privacy for Location-Based Services
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The increasing use of location-based services (LBS) poses a significant threat to location privacy of the user. The selection and transmission of dummy locations with the real location in a query has emerged as a common approach to preserve location privacy of a user in LBS. Most of the existing schemes employ entropy maximization as a metric for selecting dummy locations. However, the entropy maximization-based schemes do not preserve privacy in all cases. In this paper, we analyze the limitation of entropy maximization-based schemes in providing privacy. Further, we consider a scenario wherein a stationary user repeatedly uses LBS within a short interval of time and show the adverse impact of the repeated queries of the user on the performance of the existing scheme. We propose an enhanced scheme that preserves privacy of user even for repeated queries. Lastly, numerical results verify the performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Modeling and Performance Analysis of FFR-aided Dense Cellular Network in 3-D Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The location of base stations (BSs) and mobile users in the cellular network are typically modeled by poison point process theory considering 2-D environment. These models are suitable for the less dense rural or suburban environment, but not suitable for a dense urban environment. Moreover, with the admittance of Internet of Things (IoT), a large number of self-operating devices have started connecting over the wireless network. It necessitates the 5G wireless network to analyze the performance of the system in a more realistic three dimensions (3D) environment. In this work, we model and analyze the performance of fractional frequency reuse (FFR)-aided dense cellular network in a realistic 3-D environment. The proposed model applies to any general environment. Based on the proposed 3-D cellular network model, the coverage probability (CP) and average rate expressions are derived. Compared to traditional 2-D cell deployment, the proposed 3-D cell deployment is more accurate, and provides a closer bound of CP and average rate. It is shown that the performance of the cellular network in 2-D network overestimates the actual performance of the cellular network in 3-D environment.

articleTitle: Wideband H-shaped Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, a H-shaped dielectric resonator antenna with wide bandwidth is presented. Here, H-shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is resonating with fundamental TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup> mode with 10-dB impedance bandwidth of about 24%, at centre frequency of 4.18 GHz (3.7-4.67 GHz). The proposed design offered a gain of more than 6 dB and the radiation efficiency of more than 90% over the bandwidth of operation. The proposed antenna size is 20×20×12.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (0.278λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>×0.278λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>×0.176λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>) at 4.18 GHz. The proposed DRA is suitable for mid-band spectrum (3.7-4.2 GHz) for expanding 5G.

articleTitle: ADC Bit Allocation for massive MIMO using modified dynamic programming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: An optimal ADC Bit-Allocation (BA) Algorithm based on the maximization of the cost <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}_{f}$</tex> was derived in [1], [2]. The optimal BA ensures Minimum Mean Squared Error performance of the massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output receiver. However, this Algorithm has an additive complexity of of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N_{b}^{N_{s}})$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{b}$</tex> is the ADC bit range and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{s}$</tex> the number of RF paths. In this paper, we propose a modified dynamic programming algorithm that significantly reduces the additive complexity to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N_{b}^{2}N_{s}N_{e}^{\prime})$</tex>. Typically, dynamic programming is used to solve optimization problems with linear constraints, given the cost function satisfies the principle of optimality. Here, we modify the cost <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}_{f}$</tex> as a multi-valued function and show that it satisfies the principle of optimality under a power constraint, which is non-linear. This results in maintaining multiple winning paths (survivors) at each node in the trellis to arrive at the optimal BA solution. We also derive the minimum number of survivors <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{e}^{\prime}$</tex> required to do so. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we compare the MSE performance of the proposed algorithm with that of the algorithm in [1].

articleTitle: Application of Game Theory to Cooperative Underlay Cognitive Radio IoT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Internet of things (IoT) is a new paradigm in wireless communication that offers a host of new opportunities to exploit the finite resources available. Cognitive radio networks (CRNs) employ these spectrum opportunities by using their inherent adaptive nature to automatically detect available channels in the spectrum and change transmission parameters to allow more communications to run concurrently, thus improving overall efficiency. The application of game theoretic principles to solving problems in this domain allows for the creation of fairly realistic models that clearly outline the relationship between the stakeholders involved, under the assumption of rationality. This paper presents a model for an IoT-based CRN in the underlay mode of operation. A triangular lattice with a set of relays is considered to model the secondary user network. The interference and power constraints accounted for in calculating the Nash equilibrium bring the model closer to direct applicability in the real world by including variations depending on channel strength and desirability.

articleTitle: ABC optimization aided Joint User and Throughput Maximization in underlay D2D communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Device to Device (D2D) communication represents a paradigm shift in the quest for realizing the twin objectives of maximization of system throughput and spectral efficiency for 5G networks. D2D communication allows devices in close proximity, to directly communicate, bypassing the base station, by reusing the licensed spectral resources of the cellular users. The resulting interference between D2D and cellular users has to be controlled by intelligent resource management strategies. In this paper, we have used Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) optimization to solve the joint user selection and throughput maximization optimization problem for D2D communication underlaying cellular network. The optimization herein, represents a mixed integer nonlinear programming problem (MINLP) nondeterministic polynomial (NP) hard problem, whose computational complexity increases exponentially with the number of users. ABC optimization, based on the foraging behavior of the bees, is used to provide a solution to the optimization problem. The ABC algorithm jointly optimizes user selection, mode selection and power allocation for D2D users, subject to interference, power and quality of service (QoS) constraints. The ABC aided solution is evaluated under multiple simulation scenarios. The results obtained prove the efficacy of the ABC aided approach as compared to results reported in literature.

articleTitle: Freshness Management of Cache Content in Information-Centric Networking
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Information-Centric Networking is proffering the roadway for future internet architecture. It is a transposition from the host-centric model to a content-centric model that supports unique naming, name-based routing and in-network caching. However, managing the stale content in in-network caching is one of the research challenges. The problem becomes even more perceptible in the case of transient data where there is a stringent requirement for the freshness of information. In this paper, we posit a cache freshness mechanism for both transient and static data with minimum signaling overhead. For transient data that require live updates, data is fetched directly from the producer and no in-network caching is done. However, rest of the transient data are assigned a lifetime by the producer. Lifetime of the content in the cache is checked in case a Interest packet for the same is received by the node from the consumer which reduces the overhead. For static data the item is evicted only due to the cache eviction policy. To validate our results we simulated the work in ndnSIM, and checking the efficiency and effectiveness of the work.

articleTitle: Coverage Enhancement in Indoor Millimeter Wave Systems Under Random Human Blockages
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: To meet the demands of future indoor multi-gigabit wireless systems, millimeter wave (mm-wave) and sub-mm-wave transmissions are particularly attractive. One of the key difficulties in evaluating the performance of such systems is to take the effect of human blockages into account. In this paper, we model the human blockages of an indoor mm-wave system using tools from stochastic geometry, and thus, we provide a realistic characterization of the system performance. Then, we propose a power-partitioning scheme based on a reflective secondary path, in order to enhance the rate coverage of the system. This potentially reduces installation costs of such systems as compared to solutions present in the literature. Finally, we study the trends of the system outage and the optimal power splitting factor with varying density of blockages and transmitter positions. The framework developed in this paper can be used as a guideline for system design and installation of such systems.

articleTitle: Resource Sharing For Energy Harvesting Based D2D Communication Underlaying Cellular network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper addresses the uplink resource allocation problem for energy harvested device to device (D2D) communication. The problem is formulated to maximize the D2D throughput while considering the quality of service (QOS) for the cellular user (CU). The maximization problem is non-concave mixed integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) in nature. Thus, to reuse the resource block (RB) of CU, a heuristic approach called space matching algorithm (SMA) is deployed based on the minimum distance criteria. We estimate the total harvested energy required for D2D communication and also derive the relationship between energy harvesting efficiency factor and average percentage of active D2D pairs along with variation of total energy harvested with respect to active no of D2D pairs. We also verify our proposed scheme with the existing scheme such as JOPRA and EPA.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Heterogeneous Traffic Networks with Anarchists and Socialist Traffic
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a heterogeneous traffic network with multiple users classes which differ considerably in their path selection objective. In particular, we consider two classes of users: ones who seek to minimize social cost (socialists) and the ones with typical greedy objective (anarchists) which leads to a heterogeneous game termed as HetGame. The paper proposes an analytical framework to derive optimal/equilibrium flow in such a heterogeneous game along with a method for the same. The paper considers multiple examples of different networks to derive the optimal traffic assignment. We introduce two metrics: price of α anarchy and price of good behavior to evaluate the impact of anarchists and implications of central directives. Finally, the proposed algorithm is implemented for a real traffic network to derive insights.

articleTitle: Hybrid Modulation Scheme and Modified Energy Detector for Molecular Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: To increase the data throughout in molecular communications (MC), recently higher order modulation schemes (HOMS) are introduced with increased system complexity. In this paper, we propose a hybrid modulation scheme by encoding information into the time and types of molecules, and it is referred to as position molecule shift keying (PMSK). The PMSK uses minimum types of molecules for information encoding, which results in reduced system complexity as compared to the conventional HOMS. Further, to optimize the energy detector (ED) performance, we propose a pth power ED and call it modified ED (MED). Numerical results show that, the proposed PMSK and MED can yield higher data throughput and improved symbol error rate performance, respectively, in the presence of both counting and residual noises.

articleTitle: Error Rate Analysis and Efficient Channel Dependent Scheduling for SC-FDMA Uplink
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Multiple access techniques like single carrier frequency division multiple access (SC-FDMA) requires orthogonal subcarriers to be distributed among various active users by the base station (BS). Intelligent scheduling of available subcarriers can significantly improve the quality of service (QoS) by employing SC-FDMA for uplink mobile communication. The BS scheduler must efficiently utilize the available frequency and multi-user diversity with limited side information exchange. In this regard, a simplified mathematical approach is first discussed for symbol error rate (SER) analysis of SC-FDMA system over a generalized multipath channel utilizing the statistical characterization of effective noise after equalization. The derived expressions of SER are generalized and simplified as it only depends on the equalizer amplification factor (EAF). The analysis is then used as a quick and accurate method to compare performance over various available subbands (SB's) for subcarrier distribution by BS scheduler with less side information to be exchanged. Since the error rate is directly dependent on EAF, we have used EAF for channel-dependent scheduling (CDS) performed by the base station (BS) for SC-FDMA.

articleTitle: Rateless Code-Aided Transmission Scheme to Achieve Secrecy in a Delay-Constraint Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper analyses a secure transmission scheme using rateless codes (RC). As per the characteristic of the RC, receiver has to accumulate sufficient number of packets to reconstruct the entire source file. By utilizing the aforementioned characteristic, secure delivery can be achieved if the legitimate user accumulates required number of packets before the eavesdropper does. Thus, to expedite the decoding rate of the packets at the intended user, a two slot cooperative relaying is used. Besides, in this scheme, destination assists the source node and the source node assists the relay node in the first and the second slot respectively, to cooperatively send artificial noise without affecting the legitimate receiver. Quality of violation probability (QVP) which includes delay, reliability and secrecy is used as the performance metric, and its closed-form is derived. Both feedback-aided transmission (FT) and un-aided transmission (UT) are studied. Result shows that for FT, an increase in the total power reduces QVP, and by increasing the number of source packets intercept probability decays for both UT and FT.

articleTitle: Throughput and Service Enhancing Network Selection Algorithm for Dual Registration in 5G Standalone Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) has defined migration path from 4G (LTE) to 5G New Radio (NR) via Non Stand Alone (NSA) architecture first and then a Stand Alone (SA) architecture. SA architecture allows a User Equipment (UE) supporting both 4G and 5G, to operate in Dual Registration (DR) mode by being connected to both the networks, thus offering many advantages. However, problems could arise while facilitating a DR operation during UE network selection in the event of (i) UE powering on or performing recovery from loss of coverage to achieve dual registration mode and (ii) dual registered UE encountering temporary rejects while registering on the new network. In this paper, through analysis of two different scenarios, we establish that the current 3GPP algorithm for network selection in the aforementioned events is inefficient. We then propose a novel network selection algorithm for DR that is significantly more efficient than the 3GPP algorithm. Simulation and experiment carried out to compare the performances indicate significant improvement in average data throughput by 30algorithm for different scenarios.

articleTitle: Performance of a Leaky-Integrate-and-Fire Model vis-a-vis Measured Response of Diseased Neurons
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Information processing in the brain is still not fully understood, and in-depth theoretical and experimental studies are required in this field. An approximate but low-complexity mathematical model on membrane potential [1] is used as a potential candidate to assess model parameters from selected measured data sets available from Allen Institute of Brain Science [2]. Four different cells having epilepsy and tumor have been considered for validating the leaky-integrate- and fire model of [1]. Values of three model parameters and their statistical features are presented in detail. Closer estimates of the model parameters will help in tuning the model and thus generating spike trains closer to what are generated by biological neurons.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Lab-On-Chip Theranostic Platforms in Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Early disease detection and its diagnosis is the most crucial and significant parameter for effective treatment, for slowing down the progress of illness and also for minimizing the cost of healthcare systems. Recent technological developments in Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) along with the advancements in the Lab-on-Chip (LoC) technology and Information and Communications technologies (ICTs) have enabled the pervasive monitoring of patients. The main focus of this article is on the application of Lab-on-Chip technology in enhancing the utility of WBAN. The main components of a LoC platform have been discussed and a four-layered WBAN architecture based on the LoC theranostic platforms has been proposed in this article.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for FPGA Implementation of Register Exchange Based Viterbi Decoder and Re-Encoding based Node Synchronizer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents: (i) A novel method for VHDL implementation of register exchange based soft-hard decision Viterbi decoder in order to augment link margins available for “rover to lander” and “lander to orbiter” telemetry links and its performance evaluation and (ii) Re-encoding based node synchronizer. Register exchange method is faster and have low latency as compared to traceback method, but the main disadvantage of register exchange is that it needs large number of registers to store the decoded bits corresponding to each state in trellis. Using memory based implementation for path metric computation, survival state management and register exchange, have reduced the large number of registers requirement. Bit error rate performance evaluation of the implemented hard and soft decision decoding have been carried out by varying trellis depth and soft quantization bits. The performance and threshold evaluation for node synchronizer to decide “In-Sync”, “Out-Of-Sync” have been carried out.

articleTitle: Weighted Higher Order Detector for Diffusion based Molecular Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In diffusion-based molecular communication (MC), some of the message molecules may not reach the receiver in their expected time slot due to the diffusion process. These straying molecules from previous time slots interfere with the message molecules of the current time slot which leads to inter-symbol-interference (ISI) in MC. In this paper, we propose and analyze the weighted higher order detector for MC systems to mitigate/reduce the ISI and noise. The proposed weighted higher order sum of molecules concentration enhances the signal-to-noise ratio due to the reduced channel tail and noise effect in a frame. Further, the proposed detector does not estimate instantaneous channel impulse response at the receiver, hence, is simple and has low complexity. Numerical results show that the proposed detector performs better than the conventional direct sum detection method. The impact of diffusion coefficient, number of molecules and noise distribution on the proposed detector is also analyzed.

articleTitle: An Optimized Task Placement in Computational Offloading for Fog-Cloud Computing Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The association between the fog node and the cloud in fog-cloud computing enables task data offloading for the delay-sensitive services generated from the end-users. Limited by the computational and storage resources, it is nearly impossible to execute the entire task by itself for an end-user. In this paper, we study the cooperation among fog node and the remote cloud. The task data offloading policies becomes a challenging issue when a fog node further offloads the task data to a set of neighbor fog node. We propose a task data offloading policy to find the optimum values of the amount of the offloaded tasks to each of the neighbor fog nodes and to the cloud. Besides, where to process the tasks and how many fog nodes are required for the tasks are also important to be considered. The optimization problem is formulated as a Quadratically Constraint Quadratic Programming (QCQP) and provide a solution. The extensive simulation results show the significant performance improvement in terms of delay minimization compared with several stand-alone task data execution with the increase of traffic intensity levels.

articleTitle: DoubleTrApp: A Weak Vertex Cover based DDoS Detection and Mitigation scheme using SDN approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service Attack causes the centralized controller of a Software-Defined Network to be unreachable, bringing the entire network to a halt. In this paper, we propose a model named DoubleTrApp, which uses sFlow to classify the DDoS attack and uses OpenFlow to mitigate it on a collecting set based on the Vertex Cover Problem. This paper shows how DDoS attacks can deplete controller resources and thus DoubleTrApp provides a solution to detect a DDoS attack using some bounds on two per-flow based traffic parameters. Performance results shows that the proposed model demonstrates successful attack detection and mitigation and outperforms an OpenFlow based load-balancing mechanism.

articleTitle: On outage analysis of two user cooperative NOMA with Hybrid SWIPT protocol
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we have considered a two user cooperative NOMA scheme where the near user is equipped with multiple transmit antenna. The near user harvests energy through hybrid SWIPT protocol, and then it relays the decoded signal of the far user. We use transmit antenna selection scheme. For this system, we derived the expression for the outage probability for the near user and the far user. Also, we plot the effect of different parameters on the outage performance.

articleTitle: A Smart User-Centric Visible Light Communication system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: This paper presents a smart user-centric visible light communication (VLC) system for indoor communication application wherein the VLC transmitter dynamically changes its location in order to optimize the performance at the receiver end. The experimental set-up of the proposed smart VLC transmitter with barrier detection circuit using micro-controller and ultrasonic sensor is presented. It has been shown that high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) could be achieved with a fewer light-emitting diodes (LEDs), by using a simple hardware circuitry to get high data rate, irrespective of the location of the user.

articleTitle: Remote Attestation based Software Integrity of IoT devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Internet of Things is the new paradigm towards which the world is moving today. As these devices proliferate, security issues at these scales become more and more intimidating. Traditional approach like an antivirus does not work well with these devices and there is a need to look for a more trusted solution. For a device with reasonable computational power, we use a software trusted platform module for the cryptographic operations. In this paper, we have developed a model to remotely attest to the integrity of the processes running in the device. We have also explored the various features of the TPM (Trusted Platform Module) to gain insight into its working and also to ascertain those which can make this process better. This model depends on the server and the TPM to behave as roots of trust for this model. The client computes the HMAC (Hashed Message Authentication Code) values and appends a nonce and sends these values periodically to the server via asymmetric encryption. The HMAC values are verified by the server by comparing with its known good values (KGV) and the trustworthiness of the process is determined and accordingly an authorization response is sent.

articleTitle: Secrecy performance Analysis for Underlay Cognitive Radio Network with Optimal Antenna Selection and Generalized Receiver Selection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: We have examined the physical layer security of an underlay cognitive radio network (CRN) consisting of L legitimate receivers ( STX), a secondary transmitter ( STX), an eavesdropper (Eve), and a primary user (PU). All SRX and the PU are equipped with a single antenna while the STX and Eve are implemented with multiple antennas. The optimal antenna selection scheme (OAS) is adopted at the STX, which maximizes the secrecy capacity while a generalized receiver selection scheme is adopted at the SRX. The STX sends information to the SRX with the l<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> best signal to noise ratio (SNR). The concise expressions for exact and asymptotic secrecy outage probability (SOP) for an arbitrary number of SRX, number of transmit antenna NA, and number of eavesdropper antenna NE have derived.

articleTitle: SDR Compatible Constant Current LED Driver Circuit Design for Visible Light Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The recent need for technology towards building a flexible, reliable, and versatile software back-end for data communication saw a promising prospect with the introduction of software-defined radios (SDRs). Application of this compact device in visible light communication (VLC) bounds the researcher to a level of abstraction. Therefore, in this paper, we have proposed a simple and cost-effective light-emitting diode (LED) driver circuit design which is compatible with SDRs for easy understanding and implementation of VLC applications. The proposed LED driver circuit increases the luminaire efficiency and bandwidth at the transmitter end. A detailed step by step guide for the circuit design has been presented, as well as the transient response of current and voltage across LED up to 10 MHz is demonstrated through simulation. Further, a list of commercially available required components for fabrication of the proposed LED driver circuit is provided.

articleTitle: Ergodic Capacity Analysis of Device-to-Device MIMO Relay System with Imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this work, we consider the relay assisted multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) device-to-device (D2D) communications. We have considered the variable gain amplify-and-forward relaying protocol with effect of imperfect channel state information (CSI) cooperative system over the generalized Nakagami-m fading channel for 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation and beyond systems. MIMO antenna system require dedicated radio frequency chain for each antenna which is not feasible in practice. Hence, transmit antenna selection strategy (TAS) is employed in order to choose the transmit antenna which maximizes the received signal power. Framework for the ergodic capacity is provided for TAS based MIMO D2D cooperative system in determining the achievable throughput. Impact of system and fading parameters are highlighted over the system performance. Further, Monte-Carlo simulations are performed to validate the derived analytical expressions.

articleTitle: Performance of Battery-Assisted Energy Harvesting DF Relay over Nakagami-m Channels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the performance of the time-switching relaying (TSR) protocol in a two-hop communication link between a multiple antenna source and a multiple antenna destination through a battery assisted energy harvesting (EH) single antenna decode-and-forward relay. We assume a framework in which the EH relay augments the wireless energy harvested with energy drawn from the battery. Assuming Nakagami-m fading channels, the throughput and outage performance are analyzed. We show that how the battery energy and TSR parameter can be optimized. It is shown that when m is large, battery energy consumption is lower. The system diversity is unaffected by energy harvesting at the relay. These results are important for system designers. The derived analytical results are validated by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Operation of Energy Detector for Random Signals in Gaussian Noise
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: A simplified expression for the probability of detection and based on that a numerically solved expression for optimal power operation of improved energy detector for random signals in Gaussian noise is proposed. The expression for the optimal power operation of energy detector which maximizes the probability of detection is a function of the system settings viz. probability of false alarm, average signal to noise ratio and sample size. The expression is obtained by numerical curve fitting tool in regression analysis of MATLAB and it has 97.895% of accuracy rate on an average when it is compared with the numerical results. The expression reduces the effort to find the optimum value of power operation based on the system settings to improve the detection performance of current wireless systems, which uses the energy detector. One of such wireless system is cognitive radio, where detecting the presence of primary user signal is crucial for reliable operation.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Enhancement in Full-Duplex Relay System through Adaptive Antenna Allocation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Energy efficiency (EE) is one of the crucial parameter for designing the next generation wireless communication standard. This paper investigates the impact of antenna allocation on the EE of a full-duplex (FD) decode-and-forward (DF) relay system. Further, a scheme based on antenna allocation (AA) is proposed that enhances the EE of the FD relay system. Since the complete mitigation of self-interference (SI) in the FD system is inevitable, the SI impacts the reception at the relay, whereas the transmission from relay is relatively interference-free. The proposed scheme exploits the above and proposes an unequal antenna distribution for transmission and reception at the FD relay, wherein more number of antennas are allocated for information reception as compared to information transmission at the FD relay. The proposed AA scheme also reduces the circuit power consumption by reducing the number of active RF transmit chains at the FD relay. It has been shown that the EE can be further enhanced through adaptive AA, where the antennas are allocated based on channel gain. Good agreement between the analytically obtained expressions and simulation results validates the proposed analysis.

articleTitle: Success Probability Analysis for Edge Caching in Massive MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Edge caching is one of the promising solutions to fulfill the demands in future wireless networks. Considering a multi-cell multi-user massive MIMO (multiple-input-multiple-output) system, in this paper, we analyze average success probability (ASP) measure under the assumption of maximal ratio transmission (MRT) precoding. With respect to caching, ASP represents a measure of both the content placement and delivery performance. For the networks, where the base stations (BSs) and users are distributed as homogeneous Poisson point process (PPP), we show that for interference-limited systems, ASP is independent of the densities of both BS and users, concluding that the evaluation of a given caching scheme depends on the threshold chosen. Simulation results are presented to show the above relations.

articleTitle: Predation Blocking Strategy in Presence of Fraudulent Incumbent Service Provider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In cellular network, it is desirable to have more mobile carriers for the sake of fare pricing of network service. We assume that right to allocate bandwidth is exclusive to the Government. Government wants to maintain fair competition in the market to avoid monopoly by more powerful service provider. We consider the case where an existing dominant service provider actively tries to prevent another competitor from entering into market. The dominant service provider have larger revenue than its competitor. If the incumbent service provider can hide it's true financial data from the audit process of the Government, it can manipulate the system to successfully thwart the new competition. In this work we have shown that, Government can sell bandwidth in multiple stages and by employing proper strategy, can nullify the incumbent SP's incentive for corruption.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency of Optical Camera Communication using Dynamic Rate Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Optical Wireless Communication [OWC] involves communication over a light media by a Transmit-Receive pair. In Optical Camera communication (OCC), a camera is involved in decoding the received information while transmitter transmits the information by encoding it in a spatially arranged colour codes. If there is information loss in the received image resulting in the incorrect decoding of the received information, the overall system throughput will decrease. Information loss could be due to long distance, low camera resolution, background illumination and opaqueness of the media between the transmitter and the receiver. This paper presents a rate adaptation mechanism to improve the communication throughput by minimizing information loss. Based on our literature survey, we find that our approach is novel. We have also presented a comparative performance with and without rate adaptation. While throughput improvement with rate adaptation varies in our experiment, the maximum improvement we have achieved is by ∼50%.

articleTitle: Downlink Coverage Analysis of 3-D Ultra Dense Networks with Realistic Propagation Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this work, the analytical performance evaluation of 3-dimensional dense small cell wireless network is presented using spatial Poisson point processes. As against existing literature which considers simplified channel models without differentiating in LOS/NLOS conditions, this work captures the holistic effect of the realistic propagation (in terms of both path loss and small scale fading) as reported in existing standards. For such practical system model, a numerically simple upper bound of downlink coverage probability has been derived as a function of AP and UE densities which is found to be tight in nature for the whole range of system parameters and thus can be used as a close approximation of the same.

articleTitle: A Cross Entropy Minimization based Beam Selection for Time-Variant mmWave Beamspace MU-MIMO Communication System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The millimeter wave beamspace multi-user MIMO communication system suffers from high radio frequency complexity. However, RF complexity can be reduced by deploying a beam selection algorithm at access point without significant loss in the performance. Therefore, we proposing a novel time-variant beam selection algorithm for such system. It follows a metaheuristic approach to find the near-to-optimal solution and outperforms the existing time-variant beam selection algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancement of IEEE802.11p-based Channel Access Scheme for Internet of Vehicle (IoV)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Internet of Vehicle (IoV) aims to connect vehicles, people and things around the vehicle during the travel, which assists the driver with safety measures and increases the comfort of the passengers. To support service differentiation, IEEE802.11p protocol adopts Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) mechanism. Without knowing current queue size and network load, mapping of different priority packets to Access Category (AC) queue is a trivial task. To mitigate this, Dynamic EDCA (D-EDCA) scheme is proposed in this paper for dynamic queue allocation and optimal tuning of EDCA contention parameters. For these two functions, the proposed D-EDCA scheme utilizes run-time decision parameters such as queue access rate and current network status to achieve better performance. The simulations are carried out using NS3 with SUMO and the results are analyzed and compared with that of conventional EDCA and other similar work, A-EDCA. It is inferred from this analysis that the proposed D-EDCA outperforms better than other algorithms with respect to packet delivery ratio, queue access rate and delay of safety and non-safety messages.

articleTitle: A Score Level Fuzzy Rule based Multi-Biometric Framework for enhancing security of cloud access scenario
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: One of the major authentication threats arises at the access entrance point of the cloud which leads to the need of developing a reliable authentication framework. Multimodal authentication systems represent an emerging trend for cloud information security. Multi-modal Biometric Frameworks (MBF) utilize more than one biometric identifier to recognize a person. MBF are expected to be more reliable due to the presence of multiple independent pieces of biometric traits. The aim of these multibiometric systems is to achieve a high reliability to determine or verify person's identity. The motivation for using fuzzy logic is that it offers methods best suited to model the information that is inherently uncertain and ambiguous. This paper implements score level fusion based on fuzzy logic for developing Fuzzy Rule Based (FRB) MBF. The matching module integrates fuzzy logic methods for matching score fusion. This approach is tested on the fingerprint and face score database of 102 people obtained from NIST BSSR1 database. The experimental results exhibits that the proposed method is comparable with the existing recognizing methods. The proposed FRB MBF results in enhanced security by achieving GAR of 90.2% at FAR of 0.0029 and EER equal to 0.078.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Ego based Community Detection in Social Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Community detection or formation of clustering is a well defined problem of pattern recognition where interaction pattern of the members is measured. The detection of well defined communities are based on the fact that interaction within the community will be maximum whereas the interaction with the other communities will be minimum. Though several numbers of good community detection algorithms are present for well defined clustering, time complexity of these algorithm is quiet high and thus cannot be treated as the good measures of detection of community where number of nodes in the network is too large. In this paper, we are proposing a novel algorithm of community detection based on hierarchical ego based algorithm. In a network, ego is defined as the highest node degree centrality node and this node is treated as the cluster center of the community in our algorithm. The nodes closely connected with the ego node formed the community and from the remaining network the same process is iterated for community detection. For the result, dataset is extracted using Node-XL from a Twitter account, R based Hadoop network is used for the analysis of the network. For the visualization of the network I-graph is used.

articleTitle: Coexistence of LTE-Unlicensed and WiFi with Non-identical Contention-free Rates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this work we propose an auction-theoretic based mechanism to enable coexistence of LTE-unlicensed and WiFi. The contention-free rates that the different WiFi can achieve are allowed to be non-identical (which is in contrast to the existing models in the literature where the WiFi are assumed homogeneous). Using techniques from auction theory we characterize the solution in terms of Bayesian Nash equilibrium (BNE) bidding-strategies. We derive results illustrating the structure of a BNE strategy. We finally demonstrate the performance (in terms of achieved payoffs) of the proposed mechanism via. a detailed numerical and simulation study.

articleTitle: Group Based Semi-orthogonal User Scheduling for Massive MIMO Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Use of a huge number of base station (BS) antennas at the transmitter and a large number of active users with single transmit-receive antenna is an attractive paradigm for wireless communication. The system provides a high sum rate in a Rayleigh fading channel, the sum rate depending on how the users are scheduled for transmission by the BS antenna. In this paper, we have proposed a novel user scheduling technique which is based on dividing the users in groups using simple K-means clustering. We select users which are semi-orthogonal (SOU) to each other from the groups using two schemes. The scheme divides the number of active users Q to be scheduled by the numbers of groups G. The scheme-1 chooses one user from each group and repeats the same. The scheme-2, selects equal number of SOUs, Q/G from each group, maintaining semi-orthogonality between users from different groups and within the group. We observe that for zero-forcing (ZF) preceding, the scheme-2 provides the highest system sum rate. Moreover, we too show the results of a scheduling scheme where no grouping of users is made.

articleTitle: A Novel Key Generating Scheme of Automatic Variable Key
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The major objectives of the computer networks are, sharing information and providing uninterrupted services over a distance. Because of the critical nature of computer networks and continuous development in information technology, the probability of getting hacked and leaking of the shared message becomes a bigger threat. Therefore, achieving perfect security in such shared data is an incredible research challenge. The pioneering work of Shannon on perfect security says that shared data can only be kept confidential if the length of the key is higher or equal to the size of the message. Therefore, in this paper, we have proposed a pseudorandom function which will take negotiated session keys and data block as a seed value and produce the required number of distinct keys i.e. Automatic Variable key (AVK) for each block of data transmission instead using the same key every time.

articleTitle: SDN Based Dynamic Resource Scheduling for Large Scale Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: With the emergence of cloud computing, data centers become the core component of the underlying infrastructure. Operations of the data centers rely on resource availability, bandwidth, and efficient resource scheduling and allocation. SDN based traffic flow management approach can be used for efficient resource scheduling in the data centers by analyzing flow properties. In the past, queuing systems are being used for the assessment of the client/server model for distributed processing. In this paper, a queuing model-based algorithm is proposed for the dynamic resource scheduling for the optimization of resource requirement in data centers. The proposed algorithm takes advantage of SDN traffic flow management technique and finds the optimal number of servers for a data center to reduce the operational cost of the system. The proposed model reduces the required number of servers in the system to achieve a service throughput and is able to cater to various type of requests. In this work a single M|M|c system model is divide into multiple M|M|c sub-systems to optimize the required number of servers. And incoming traffic is divided into different service classes. This model is tested for SDN and the simulation results validate the efficacy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: On Achieving Hidden Markov Model Estimation Freshness in Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Various state estimation problems in dairy farm applications, like heat detection, feeding behavior, etc. are well studied by using Hidden Markov Models (HMM) to represent the sampled process. Our use-case of monitoring cows in remote farms in real-time and perform online state estimation/classification requires intelligent sampling of the underlying HMM. Due to the limited capacity of the sensor network at the dairy farm, and due to possible wireless errors, the central server does not always receive all the sampled data. Right value of the observation arrival rate into the parameter and state estimation algorithm running at a central server is required to ensure that a prescribed heat detection performance level is achieved. We provide a working implementation of a setup where the end devices using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) are provided with an online recommendation on the sampling (hence, channel access) rates so that the HMM state estimated at the central server is ( α, β)-current.

articleTitle: Re-synchronization in a Synchronized IEEE 802.15.4 Cluster-tree Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In an IEEE 802.15.4 cluster tree network, a synchronization scheme achieves beacon synchronization among coordinators that allow devices to schedule their beacons in a non-overlapping way. This prevents unnecessary data frame collisions as well as allows devices to enter sleep periods, thereby increasing the overall network performance and lifetime, respectively. Synchronization schemes proposed in the literature primarily focused on either schedulability, overhead, or MAC goodput. But, none of these schemes analyze the factors that may affect synchronization among the devices. In this paper, we identify and analyze the impact of such factors and show that the absence of mechanisms to handle the issue of loss of synchronization will result in high network overhead. Since the goal of a low-rate wireless network (based on IEEE 802.15.4 standard) is to maximize network lifetime, it is highly desirable to explore all possible energy-conserving avenues and address them. In this regard, we propose lightweight re-synchronization mechanisms that address the issue of lost synchronization with minimal overhead.

articleTitle: Test-bench for Task Offloading Mechanisms: Modelling the Rewards of Non-stationary Nodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a framework to model the server nodes' non-stationary reward distribution as an N-state Markov chain derived from the long-term probability distribution of the reward, in which the state transitions occur at an interval defined as a non-homogeneous Poisson process. The framework aims to serve as a tool for validation and as a test-bench for comparing the performance of various learning algorithms in non-stationary bandits and similar applications where the server nodes' computational reward distribution is dynamic.

articleTitle: Wideband mmWave Massive MIMO Channel Estimation Using Stagewise Weak Conjugate Gradient Pursuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Meeting the demand for high-speed communication requires exploiting new frequencies and developing novel technologies. Massive MIMO and mmWave communication promise to significantly increase the overall system capacity. The communication utilizing these bands suffers from the problem of path loss which can severely downgrade the strength of the transmitted signal. However, the use of hybrid beamforming and effective high-speed channel estimation algorithm can help to tackle this problem and to invent the necessitated communication system for 5G. Our main focus in this paper is to obtain the most effective channel estimation algorithm in term of the computational time and the achievable capacity. We propose a new algorithm and make a comparison with several greedy and iterative hard thresholding algorithms. The results show that our proposed algorithm Stagewise Weak Conjugate Gradient Pursuit (SWCGP) is the most efficient algorithm such that this algorithm makes a tradeoff between the execution time (speed) and the attainable capacity.

articleTitle: Performance of Random Access Games over an IEEE 802.11ac Testbed
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: It is well known that the wireless networks following the IEEE 802.11 standard do not achieve high throughput and short-term fairness when the network size is large. Many game-theoretic random access MAC protocols have been proposed to address this limitation. Performance of game-theory based protocols can be precisely analyzed, predicted and tuned unlike protocols based on purely ad-hoc arguments. In this paper, we implement game-theoretic CSMA MAC protocols in an indoor IEEE 802.11ac wireless network testbed. We perform extensive experiments for various network configurations. Measurements indicate that the game-based models achieve higher average throughput, lower access delay and lower access delay deviation compared to the standard DCF algorithm.

articleTitle: An Online Algorithm for Energy Harvesting Cognitive Radio IoT Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Increase in Internet of Things (IoT) applications rise the demand for more wireless connectivity. One of the promising solutions is to utilize the unused licensed Television White Spaces (TVWS) spectrum. In this paper, we consider energy harvesting cognitive radio wireless network operators (ECTNOs) which use TV white spaces (TVWS) for wireless connectivity. These network operators harvest RF energy and use it for transmission purpose. Spectrum leasing is considered essential to support wide range of IoT applications. We have considered two types of spectrum availability: free TVWS and High Priority Channels (HPCs) of TVWS to be taken on lease. We propose an online algorithm for energy harvesting cognitive radio IoT network to optimize the cost with respect to data quality and transmission delay. There is trade-off between total system cost and these QoS parameters. The performance of the proposed energy harvesting online algorithm is seen to be consistent with the optimal algorithm in non energy harvesting case.

articleTitle: A study of Average and Peak Age-of-Information for MAC protocols in Contiki
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Contiki is a popular internet of things (IoT) operating system (OS) which supports a wide variety of low-cost, low-power IoT devices. IoT wireless networks which are comprised of devices running the Contiki OS can be used to collect time-sensitive data from sensors to a central station. The quality of service performance of such wireless networks depends on the multiple access protocol (MAC) implementations within the Contiki OS. An important quality of service performance metric for IoT and sensor networks is Age-of-Information (AoI) which measures the freshness of the collected information. In this paper, we study the average and peak AoI performance of a single hop wireless network containing Sky mote devices which run the Contiki OS for multiple in-built MAC protocols. We also implement time-division MAC as well as a hybrid MAC protocol in Contiki and study the average and peak AoI performance. The measurement studies are done in the Cooja wireless network simulator.

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Management System Based on Software Defined Internet of Things Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)

authors.preferredName: Venkata Sai Surya Laxman Rao Bellala

abstract: Rising traffic congestion is an inescapable condition in large and growing metropolitan cities leading to many problems for an individual or group. Movement of emergency vehicles are hampered due to traffic congestion costing lives. This work aims to provide a solution to the Road Traffic Management System in order to avoid congestion and to provide services in an emergency situation. This work uses the emerging paradigm in the network called Software Defined Networks (SDN), also known as Network Automation and Network Programmability, to solve traffic congestion. In this work, we have used a real - life model, borrowed from the state of Orissa and the city of Bhubaneshwar, to develop an application for managing the traffic congestion. This application is built using the Software Defined Internet of Things (SDIoT) architecture. Our work highlights the need for SDN in IoT.

articleTitle: Reliable Transmission of Critical Packets in IEEE 802.15.4-based Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a mechanism to ensure reliable transmission of critical packets in Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs). As WBANs are responsible for real-time health monitoring, thus, high success rate is necessary in packet transmissions. Especially, packets that possess critical health information must be dealt with utmost priority. To ensure this, in this work we express the probability of successful packet transmission as a function of maximum number of backoff stage - an important MAC parameter - so that we can judiciously tune its value to achieve maximum transmission reliability for critical nodes. The IEEE 802.15.4 is used as the underlying communication standard. We use a simple two-dimensional Markov chain to model the slotted CSMA-CA based channel access mechanism of IEEE 802.15.4, which acts as the basis of the whole work. We compare the proposed approach with random assignment of maximum number of backoff stage to the body sensor nodes and show that judicious tuning of this value yields 25% improvement in reliable packet transmission, in comparison with random assignment.

articleTitle: Handling concurrent requests in a secret sharing based storage system using Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Data can be stored securely in various storage servers. But in the case of a server failure, or data theft from a certain number of servers, the remaining data becomes inadequate for use. Data is stored securely using secret sharing schemes, so that data can be reconstructed even if some of the servers fail. But not much work has been carried out in the direction of updation of this data. This leads to the problem of updation when two or more concurrent requests arrive and thus, it results in inconsistency. Our work proposes a novel method to store data securely with concurrent update requests using Petri Nets, under the assumption that the number of nodes is very large and the requests for updates are very frequent.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Architectures for Modeling Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Recently, deep learning for physical layer has been modeled using autoencoders to model the entire communication system end-to-end. We extend these methods to improve the overall performance by adopting various learning strategies when multiple users try to communicate over a shared channel. We consider cooperative and non-cooperative schemes in the 2-user Gaussian interference channel. Additionally, a simple neural network architecture is provided for wireless communication systems where channel gain matrix either attenuates or, in some cases, results in fading of the message signal sent by the transmitter.

articleTitle: Light-weight, Real-time Internet Traffic Classification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The identification of TCP applications associated with Internet traffic is an essential step to apply quality-of-service policies, to monitor network usage for resource allocation at the server, and to maintain the security and integrity of those resources. However, one of the prime challenges posed by Internet traffic classification is its early identification, i.e., identifying a TCP application without having to go through the entire traffic flow. We work in this direction and propose a light-weight classifier that exploits the behaviour associated with different applications. In particular, our method uses the size of the first five packets of an Internet connection to classify the TCP application associated with it, using K-means clustering. Overall our classifier is simple, computationally light-weight, and can classify traffic in real-time with 97.68% accuracy. Moreover, it can also support high-speed links, detect potential new applications, and peer-to-peer traffic.

articleTitle: Phase-noise Impact on the Performance of mmWave-radars
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The impact of phase noise in Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) millimeter-wave (mmWave) radars is investigated in this paper. A FMCW signal is transmitted from the radar, reflected off a moving object and processed at a receiver in the radar. The impact of random phase noise/jitter on the performance parameters of estimated distance, speed and angle of arrival of an object is studied. Our studies show that there exists a threshold at about fifteen percent of the period of the carrier frequency, over which errors substantially manifest in the estimations. Distance estimation is less affected than speed and angle, which rely directly on the phase information for the estimations. Angle estimation error is particularly sensitive to noise when the angle of the object exceeds ±70 degrees.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of SM-based Hybrid MIMO FSO/RF System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Free space optical (FSO) communication has emerged as an alternative technology to conventional RF technology for the abundance of unregulated spectrum, high immunity to electromagnetic interference and high security. But unlike RF technology, it's highly sensitive to atmospheric turbulence. A communication system comprising of both FSO and RF technologies can reap benefits from both. We propose a hybrid SM-based FSO/RF model to increase the throughput and reliability of the system. The FSO channel is modelled as Malaga- M distributed and RF channel is assumed to be Nakagami- m distributed. Spatial modulation (SM) at the transmitter is incorporated to increase the spectral efficiency and selection combiner is employed at the receiver to achieve higher diversity order. Monte Carlo simulation of ergodic capacity and symbol error rate (SER) has been carried out.

articleTitle: Vector-Valued KLMS based Multiple Target Range and Velocity Estimation using IEEE 802.11p Waveform for Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: An autonomous vehicle equipped with radar is used to monitor the movement of other vehicles (targets) in the vicinity. Radars on autonomous vehicles are primarily used for accurate estimation of targets' (neighboring vehicles) range and velocity to avoid collision and fatal accidents. The existing linear estimator based on Fourier transform, in the multi-target scenario, is prone to yield inaccurate estimates of targets' parameters. In this paper, to jointly estimate the range and velocity of multiple vehicles, an adaptive non-linear estimator based on vector-valued kernel least mean square algorithm is proposed. The proposed estimator optimizes the convex cost function in reproducing kernel Hilbert space and consequently yields better estimates. Further, the complexity of the proposed estimator is reduced by incorporating the sparsification technique. Analytical expressions for Cramer-Rao lower bound are derived to evaluate the performance of the proposed estimator. Lastly, simulation results validate the performance of the proposed estimator via convergence to a lower normalized mean square error with reasonable computational complexity.

articleTitle: Null Steering and Sidelobe Canceller using Frequency Response Masking approach for Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Interference is the primary factor limiting the performance of communication systems for military as well as commercial communication applications. This paper proposes methods to reduce the effects of interference by estimating the Direction of Arrival (DOA) of the interferers and introducing nulls in the direction of the interferers for uniform linear antenna arrays. This approach nullifies the effects of the interferer, leading to enhanced performance of communication systems. The Frequency Response Masking (FRM) approach is used to synthesize the antenna pattern of the uniform linear array beamformer to reject the effects of the interfering signals. The resulting antenna pattern places the nulls in the direction of the interferers and reduces the amplitude of the sidelobes. The proposed method provides a tradeoff between the width of the mainlobe and the height of the sidelobes, leading to the generation of antenna patterns with narrow mainlobes, lower sidelobes as well as rejection of interferers. Simulation results prove the efficacy of the FRM approach for interference rejection and sidelobe cancellation.

articleTitle: Determination of Participating Nodes in Opportunistic Networks for VANET
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Opportunistic networks offer an innovative solution that enables fast transmission of messages based on the amount of interaction between the nodes. This work is focused on classifying the nodes based on their willingness to forward messages to any destination. Memory constraints and social interaction features are considered to be attributes in finding their interest in forwarding messages. `Multiple Classifiers Approach' is adopted to ascertain the nodes that are available for participation in the message transmission of Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). The classifiers used in this approach are the `Naive Bayes Classifier' and the `Multi-Layer Perceptron Classifier'. Reachability among nodes is assessed using the number of participating nodes in Opportunistic Networks. The Naïve Bayes Classifier produced an accuracy of around 86% when determining the nodes available for participation in the VANET system while the Multi-Layer Perceptron Classifier produced an accuracy of around 87% for the same. This paper gives a detailed account of the classification of nodes and the simulation of the message transmission in a VANET system. The simulation was carried out using the NS2 simulator and SUMO.

articleTitle: Visible Light Communication Modulation Toolkit using Reconfigurable GNU Radio Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a user-centric simulation platform for indoor visible light communication (VLC) systems using open source GNU Radio framework. The three standard VLC modulation schemes, on-off keying (OOK), direct current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM) and asymmetrically clipped OFDM (ACO-OFDM) are investigated. The state-of-the art modulation toolkit provides a universal interface to the user to analyze the realistic performance of the three modulation schemes OOK, DCO-OFDM and ACO-OFDM in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) under different channel conditions.

articleTitle: SINR based Uplink Sub-band Clustering Mechanism for Differentiated Services in NOMA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is a contender for 5G wireless networks, since it supports large number of devices to transmit simultaneously over the same radio resource, e.g., sub-band. NOMA is particularly suitable for applications, such as, Internet of Things (IoT), where many devices contend for scarce radio resources. NOMA random access allows any device to choose a sub-band randomly to transmit data. This may lead to multiple interferers if many devices (which are not spatially dispersed) access the same sub-band. This paper proposes a novel mechanism for uplink sub-band clustering based on measured Signal to Interference and Noise Ratio (SINR) over a period of time at the base-station. The proposed mechanism can be used to provide differentiated services to the devices, which is not possible in NOMA random access proposed in literature. Simulation results show that the proposed idea suggests suitable sub-bands to devices for providing differential services.

articleTitle: Time Allocation and Scheduling in Energy Harvesting Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: The increasing demand for data services has given rise to efficient utilization of available resources (e.g., energy) in modern wireless communication. In order to address the energy requirements a wireless powered communication network (WPCN) with separate energy source (ES) and access point (AP) is considered in this work. The transmitters here adopt harvest-then-transmit (HTT) protocol for transmission to AP. An optimal dynamic time allocation and scheduling policy is considered which maximizes the throughput of the system. The throughput maximization problem formulated is convex in nature and solved using convex optimization techniques. The fairness of proposed policy is compared with max-min policy which use harvest-or-transmit (HOT) protocol in terms of Jain's fairness index. Simulation results highlights the trade-off between throughput and fairness and show that the proposed policy is more reliable for the overcrowded scenario.

articleTitle: Inferring Occupants Count from Low Power IP based Devices in Building through Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Networks and Telecommunications Systems (ANTS)
abstract: Building automation and building climate control efficiency can be improved by applying accurate occupancy information into the building management system.
